purpose: Evaluate whether explicitly marginalizing over paleomagnetic chronology uncertainty improves inference versus fixed-age plug-in baselines on synthetic known-truth trajectories.

research_reference.title: Joint Bayesian inference of Earth's magnetic field and core surface flow on millennial timescales
research_reference.reported_scope: Joint geomagnetic-field and core-surface-flow reconstruction over up to 9000 years with synthetic Earth-like geodynamo validation and discrete marginalization of chronological uncertainty.
research_reference.reuse_boundary: Use bibliographic metadata and independently authored benchmark definitions. Do not copy figures/text or publish derivative versions of the article under this benchmark manifest.

model_contract.age_support: ordered discrete ages before a named reference epoch
model_contract.weights: finite, non-negative probabilities summing to one within a documented tolerance
model_contract.likelihood: p(y|theta) = sum_j w_j * p(y|f(theta, age_j), observation_uncertainty)
model_contract.log_likelihood: logsumexp(log(w_j) + log_likelihood_at_age_j), skipping zero-weight candidates without evaluating log(0)
model_contract.forbidden_substitution: Do not replace the age-marginalized likelihood with evaluating the physical trajectory only at the mean or MAP age; treat those as explicit baseline methods.
separate_processes: physical field/core-flow prior and temporal covariance
derived field and flow state estimates
model_contract.clock_rule: Age-before-present support is not Unix time. The reference epoch and chronology model are mandatory provenance.

synthetic_scenario_families: nonlinear field evolution where mean-age plug-in is biased
sediment lock-in lag separated from chronology uncertainty
spatially uneven observations and missing intervals
baselines: single sampled age with declared random seed
metrics: held-out log predictive density or marginal log score
CRPS or another justified proper scoring rule
field-coefficient and core-flow bias/RMSE against known truth
90% and 95% empirical interval coverage with sample counts and uncertainty bounds
calibration stratified by chronology width and multimodality
false-positive rate on shuffled-age and invalid-support negative controls
runtime and memory scaling with number of candidate ages
test_protocol: Freeze simulation truth, sample-level age distributions, sensor/measurement noise, model configuration and contiguous temporal folds in a manifest.
Run exact tiny finite-support cases against a direct high-precision sum and a stable log-sum-exp result.
Include a nonlinear trajectory fixture where mean-age and MAP-age evaluation are measurably different from marginalized likelihood.
Use multiple simulation seeds and temporal holdouts; do not randomly split adjacent correlated time samples and label them independent.
Keep truth state, chronology metadata, synthetic observations, inference output and posterior chronology as distinct artifacts.
Retain every negative-control result and pin outputs to exact model/configuration/input manifest IDs.
initial_acceptance_gates: Invalid, unnormalized, negative or non-finite chronology weights fail closed.
Marginal log likelihood matches reference tiny-case calculations within a declared floating-point tolerance.

On the preregistered synthetic corpus, discrete marginalization improves held-out proper scores over at least the mean-age and MAP-age baselines without worsening declared interval-calibration tolerances.
Nominal 90% and 95% interval coverage is reported with uncertainty bounds; threshold bands must be declared before scoring, not selected after results are seen.
Shuffled chronology associations and invalid clock/reference epochs are rejected or perform no better than the predeclared null baseline.
No synthetic success is described as proof of real-Earth accuracy.
